COT: Positioning ahead of the stock market rout reveals growing caution.

💵 Dollar longs +13% to USD 32.6bn, with AUD shorts hitting a record.

🥇 Metals bear the brunt: Gold longs at a five-month low, silver virtually neutral and copper longs at a 14-month low.

🛢️ Commodity selling extends into a tenth week, with energy under pressure and grain selling finally slowing.

With the worst of the equity rout occurring after Tuesday's reporting cut-off, next week's data could reveal further liquidation.

The silver lining? Reduced speculative exposure may eventually provide a foundation for recovery.

Read our latest COT update 👇 https://t.co/vwvp7jGPy4

Crude update: For once, energy is not the main news generator across the commodity sector, with Brent trading in a relatively narrow range in the low USD 90s. Attention remains divided between recovering supply, with the IEA forecasting a surplus of roughly 2 million barrels per day this quarter, and the risk of renewed geopolitical escalation as Iran remains effectively cut off from crude exports.
The immediate focus has shifted to reports that Iran is preparing a convoy of around 14 tankers to challenge the US naval blockade of Kharg Island, its main oil export hub. President Trump has responded with a stark warning, raising the stakes of a potentially dangerous confrontation. How the US Navy responds if the convoy attempts to breach the blockade could set the tone for oil prices and geopolitical risk premiums for the remainder of the year.
Meanwhile, from an inflation perspective, the more encouraging development has been the sharp decline in refined fuel prices, particularly distillates, with London gasoil trading around USD 157 per barrel, down from approximately USD 200 at the start of the month. This easing in diesel prices could help alleviate inflation pressures and, in turn, reduce concerns about further interest rate hikes, provided the standoff with Iran does not trigger another supply disruption.

Precious metals are trading sharply higher in early Monday trading, supported by a recovery in equities and oversold conditions following last week's steep selloff. While concerns about further rate hikes, now moderating following the stock market rout, and negative momentum encouraged additional short selling, last week's weakness was primarily a liquidity-driven event. The unwinding of the AI investment theme triggered market turmoil and heavy losses, forcing investors to reduce risk across asset classes, including metals.

Gold is up 2.4% at USD 3,625, silver has gained 3.6% to USD 42.65, while copper has only managed to recover around 1% following last week's slump to an eight-month low due to several bearish drivers, including China, US tariff and AI spending concerns.

Looking ahead, sentiment remains fragile, with a sustained recovery likely requiring continued stability in equity markets and an easing of dollar and funding pressures. For now, the rebound looks more like a relief rally from oversold levels than a decisive reversal, with further gains needed to restore confidence and attract fresh buying.

Commodities: Speculative selling extends into a tenth week as metals bear the brunt

The latest COT report, covering managed money positioning across key commodity futures in the week to Tuesday, 17 November, showed continued risk reduction across most sectors, particularly metals, ahead of a brutal end to the week.

The combination of a dash for cash, dollar strength, rising US rate expectations and growing concerns about the AI investment boom was already weighing heavily on precious and industrial metals. Selling pressure accelerated sharply after Tuesday's reporting cut-off, suggesting the latest positioning data may understate the extent of the subsequent liquidation.

Overall, while the Bloomberg Commodity Index suffered a relatively modest 1% decline during the reporting week, before tumbling in the days that followed, the combined net long across the 25 major commodity futures tracked in this report fell for a tenth consecutive week, albeit at a much slower pace than in previous weeks. The aggregate net long declined by 32,377 contracts to 474,100, with selling once again concentrated in energy and, increasingly, metals.

The combined net long across 25 major commodity futures declined by 32k contracts to 474k, with selling slowing compared with previous weeks.

Metals bore the brunt:
Gold net long -9% to 104k contracts, a five-month low.
Silver's remaining net long virtually wiped out, leaving just 17 contracts.
Copper net long -21% to 27k, a 14-month low, down from 82k in September.

Energy: Combined Brent and WTI longs fell by 10k contracts to 203k amid growing concerns about a 2027 supply surplus. Gasoline longs fell 8%, while moderate short covering reduced the substantial natural gas net short by 5%.

Agriculture: Aggressive grain selling finally slowed, leaving the combined net long across six contracts at just 15k, down from around one million two months ago. Corn and both wheat contracts remain net short.

Softs: Cocoa and coffee attracted limited speculative buying despite strong price gains, while sugar and cotton saw further long liquidation.

The subsequent collapse in AI-related equities, stronger dollar, rising funding costs and broader dash for cash point to further liquidation that may become visible in next week's report.

The silver lining? Ten consecutive weeks of selling have substantially reduced speculative exposure, potentially laying the groundwork for a recovery once dollar liquidity pressures ease and attention returns to underlying supply constraints and supportive fundamentals.
